prompt: `final int maxLoans = 3;` and then `maxLoans = 4;`. What does `javac` say?
hint: Assigned exactly once.

choices.text: `cannot assign a value to final variable maxLoans`
choices.why: Right: a final variable is assigned once, and this is the second time.

choices.text: Nothing: `final` only matters for fields
choices.why: It works on locals too; `Locals.java` did not compile.

choices.text: A warning, and the variable keeps 3
choices.why: It is an error, not a warning, and nothing runs.

prompt: `Book` has `final String isbn;` and a constructor `Book(String title)` that sets only the title. Where does the error point?
hint: Where does the constructor end without having set it?

choices.text: At the declaration `final String isbn;`
choices.why: The declaration is fine; the fault is in a constructor that leaves it unset.

choices.text: At the line `this.title = title;`
choices.why: That line is correct; the problem is what is missing after it.

choices.text: At the constructor's closing brace
choices.why: Right: line 13, `variable isbn might not have been initialized`.

choices.text: At the first `new Book(...)` in another class
choices.why: The class itself does not compile, so no caller is examined.

prompt: `final StringBuilder note = new StringBuilder("Due");` Which line then compiles?
hint: `final` fixes the variable, not the object.

choices.text: `note.append(" on Friday");`
choices.why: Right: the object changes, the reference does not, and `Notes` printed `Due on Friday`.

choices.text: `note = new StringBuilder("Overdue");`
choices.why: That points the variable at another object, which `Reassign` showed is refused.

choices.text: `note = null;`
choices.why: `null` is a different reference too; a final variable takes one assignment.

prompt: A class has `private final int[] scores;` set in its constructor and returned by a getter. Can callers change the scores?
hint: What does the getter hand out?

choices.text: No: `private` and `final` together make the array unchangeable
choices.why: They make the field unassignable from outside; the array the field leads to is untouched by either.

choices.text: Yes: what it returns leads to the same array, so `[0] = 9` alters it
choices.why: Right: as `counts[0] = 9` did in `Notes`; lesson 22 shows the defensive copy that closes this.

choices.text: Only if they also have write access to the field
choices.why: They need no access to the field once they hold a reference to the array.

prompt: A `final` field with no value in its declaration, which every constructor must set, is called a blank ___.
hint: The keyword itself.

prompt: `Item` declares `final String label()`, and `Dvd extends Item` declares its own `label()`. What happens?
hint: A final method may not be replaced.

choices.text: `Dvd`'s version runs for DVDs and `Item`'s for everything else
choices.why: That is what overriding would do, and `final` forbids it.

choices.text: `Dvd` does not compile: the method is final
choices.why: Right: `label() in Dvd cannot override label() in Item`.

choices.text: `Item`'s version always runs and `Dvd`'s is silently ignored
choices.why: Nothing is ignored in silence; the compiler refuses the class.

prompt: What does `final class Isbn` forbid?
hint: `FakeIsbn` tried it.

choices.text: Making more than one `Isbn` object
choices.why: `final` on a class is about subclasses; you can make as many objects as you like.

choices.text: Changing the `value` of an `Isbn`
choices.why: That is the `final` on the field; the class's `final` is a separate thing.

choices.text: Any class that extends it
choices.why: Right: `cannot inherit from final Isbn`.

choices.text: Calling its methods from another package
choices.why: That would be access, lesson 14, not `final`.

prompt: Why does the section say `String` must be final for its promise to hold?
hint: What could a subclass add?

choices.text: Because final classes run faster, and strings are used everywhere
choices.why: Speed is not the argument the section makes.

choices.text: A subclass could change its characters, so a string checked once might differ when used
choices.why: Right: a promise a subclass can break holds for no `String` at all.

choices.text: Because `javap` would otherwise show its private fields
choices.why: `javap` shows what it shows either way; that is not the reason.

prompt: Which of these did `javac` refuse in section 03? Choose all that apply.
hint: Three refusals, and one class compiled.

choices.text: `class Dvd extends Item` overriding a final `label()`
choices.why: Yes: `overridden method is final`.

choices.text: `class FakeIsbn extends Isbn`
choices.why: Yes: `Isbn` is a final class.

choices.text: `class MyString extends String`
choices.why: Yes: `String` is final in the JDK itself.

choices.text: `final class Isbn` with a `final String value` field
choices.why: That class compiled; only its would-be subclass failed.

prompt: You want a method that does something new to strings. `String` is final. Where does the method go?
hint: Lesson 15's `Isbns`.

choices.text: In a subclass of `String`
choices.why: That is exactly what `final` refuses.

choices.text: In a static helper of your own class, given the text as a parameter
choices.why: Right: like `Isbns.looksValid(String)`.

choices.text: Into `java.lang.String` itself, after editing the JDK's source
choices.why: The JDK you run is not yours to edit, and every other machine would lack the method.

prompt: When is a local variable *effectively final*?
hint: No keyword is involved.

choices.text: When it is declared inside `main`
choices.why: Where it is declared does not matter; whether it is assigned again does.

choices.text: When nothing assigns it after its declaration
choices.why: Right: even with no `final` written.

choices.text: When it holds an object rather than a primitive
choices.why: `count` was an `int` and the rule applied to it.

choices.text: When the compiler has inlined its value as a constant
choices.why: That is lesson 15's compile-time constant, a different thing.

prompt: The second `Capture` assigned `branch = "Norte";` after making the `Runnable`. What happened?
hint: The error names an inner class.

choices.text: It printed `Report for Norte`
choices.why: It never ran: the compiler refused it.

choices.text: It printed `Report for Centro`, the value when the object was made
choices.why: That is what the copy would have printed, which is the disagreement the rule prevents.

choices.text: It did not compile
choices.why: Right: `branch` was no longer effectively final.

prompt: Why does Java forbid assigning a captured local variable again, rather than letting the inner code see the new value?
hint: What does the object keep: the variable, or its value?

choices.text: The object keeps only a copy of the value
choices.why: Right: the frame is gone by the time it runs, and a later change would leave the copy and the variable disagreeing in silence.

choices.text: Because locals are stored in the class file, which cannot change
choices.why: Locals live in a frame on the stack; the class file holds bytecode.

choices.text: To make anonymous classes run faster than ordinary methods
choices.why: Speed is not the reason; consistency is.

prompt: Does the lambda in `Lambda.java` meet the same rule as the anonymous class in `Capture.java`?
hint: Compare the two error messages.

choices.text: No: lambdas may capture any local variable
choices.why: `count = 5;` made the lambda fail to compile.

choices.text: Yes: both refuse a captured local that is assigned again
choices.why: Right: the two messages differ in one phrase, `inner class` against `lambda expression`.

choices.text: Only for primitives such as `int`
choices.why: `branch` was a `String`, and the rule applied to it as well.

prompt: Put the events of the first `Capture` in order.
hint: The copy is taken when the object is made.
items: The `Runnable` object is made, keeping a copy of `branch`

prompt: Match each use of `final` to what it forbids.
hint: Three places, three meanings.

pairs.right: Leaving it unset in a constructor, or assigning it later

right_distractors: Changing the object the variable leads to

prompt: A `Loan` should never change its book once made. Which declaration does that, and checks it at compile time?
hint: Every constructor sets it, nothing assigns it after.

choices.text: `Book book;` with a comment saying not to change it
choices.why: A comment is not checked by anything.

choices.text: `static Book book;`
choices.why: Static would give every loan the same book, which is a different bug.

choices.text: `private final Book book;`, set in every constructor
choices.why: Right: the compiler refuses a constructor that forgets it and any later assignment.

choices.text: `final class Book`
choices.why: That stops subclasses of `Book`; it says nothing about which book a loan holds.

prompt: Which of these is true of `final StringBuilder note`?
hint: Section 02's `Notes`.

choices.text: Its text can never change
choices.why: `append` changed it, and the program printed `Due on Friday`.

choices.text: It is a compile-time constant copied into other classes
choices.why: Only primitives and strings with values known at compile time are; this is an object made by `new`.

choices.text: It always leads to the same object
choices.why: Right: the reference is fixed; the object's contents are not.

prompt: `final int[] counts = {1, 2, 3}; counts[0] = 9;` What did `Notes` print for `counts[0]`?
hint: The array is not final; the variable is.

prompt: When does the section advise making one of your own classes `final`?
hint: Was it designed to be extended?

choices.text: Never: only the JDK's classes should be final
choices.why: The section advises the opposite for classes you did not design for extension.

choices.text: Unless you designed it to be extended
choices.why: Right: lesson 20 shows what extending safely asks of a class.

choices.text: Whenever it has a `final` field
choices.why: A final field and a final class protect different things.

choices.text: Only when it has static methods
choices.why: Static methods have nothing to do with being extended.
